# package mqtt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-otfp/protocols/mqtt"
```

Package mqtt fingerprints MQTT brokers.

Detection sends one CONNECT — MQTT 3.1.1 (protocol level 4), a clean session, a 10-second keep-alive, a random client identifier, no will and no credentials — and accepts only a strict CONNACK: packet type 2 with zero flags, a remaining length of 2, zero reserved acknowledge flags and a return code of 0..5. A refusal (bad credentials, not authorised, unacceptable protocol version) proves an MQTT broker as well as an acceptance does. An accepted session is cross-checked with PINGREQ / PINGRESP and closed with DISCONNECT.

An MQTT 5-only broker may close the connection on a 3.1.1 CONNECT instead of refusing it. Detection retries with an MQTT 5 CONNECT only on the well-known ports 1883 and 8883 (or in identify mode): elsewhere a silent close is far more likely a service that is not MQTT, and a second connection to every such endpoint would double the probe's footprint.

Identify mode connects with MQTT 5 first, to read the CONNACK properties (Assigned Client Identifier, Server Keep Alive, Maximum Packet Size, Receive Maximum, Retain/Wildcard/Shared Subscription Available, Topic Alias Maximum, Response Information, Server Reference, Reason String), and falls back to 3.1.1 when the broker refuses or closes. When the scan allows read-only probes it subscribes, at QoS 0, to $SYS/broker/version (the Eclipse broker and compatible ones retain it) and $SYS/brokers/+/version (EMQX), waits a short bounded window for the value, unsubscribes and disconnects. Nothing is ever published.

```go
const (
	PortTCP = 1883
	PortTLS = 8883

```

The well-known ports: MQTT over TCP and over TLS.

```go
const DefaultMaxPacket = 64 * 1024
```

DefaultMaxPacket bounds the packets the fingerprinters read: a broker's CONNACK, SUBACK and retained $SYS values are far smaller.

```go
const KeepAlive = 10
```

KeepAlive is the keep-alive, in seconds, of the CONNECTs the fingerprinters send: a session lasts a few seconds at most.

```go
const MaxRemaining = 268435455
```

MaxRemaining is the largest remaining length a four-byte variable byte integer encodes (268435455).

## Functions

### func AppendVarint

```go

```

AppendVarint appends v as a variable byte integer. v is clamped to 0..MaxRemaining.

### func ClientID

```go
func ClientID() string
```

ClientID returns a random client identifier, "otfp" and 16 hexadecimal digits: 20 characters of \[0-9a-z], which every MQTT 3.1.1 broker must accept, and unlikely to take over another client's session.

### func Connect

```go
func Connect(level byte, clientID string, keepAlive uint16) []byte
```

Connect returns a CONNECT packet of protocol level (Level311 or Level5) with a clean session, the given keep-alive and client identifier, no will and no credentials. An MQTT 5 CONNECT carries no properties.

### func Disconnect

```go
func Disconnect() []byte
```

Disconnect is the DISCONNECT packet (normal disconnection in MQTT 5).

### func Framer

```go
func Framer(limit int) wire.Framer
```

Framer returns a wire.Framer that reads one MQTT control packet of at most limit bytes (header included). A reserved packet type, flags MQTT forbids for the type, a five-byte remaining length or a packet larger than limit stop the read.


IsUnsuback reports whether p is the UNSUBACK of packet identifier id.


LevelName returns "3.1.1" or "5.0".

### func ParseSuback

```go

```

ParseSuback validates p as the SUBACK of packet identifier id with one code per filter, and returns the codes (0x00..0x02 granted QoS, 0x80 and above refusals).


PeekTopic returns the topic of a PUBLISH whose bytes may be cut short (an oversized packet the read stopped in): only the fixed header and the topic name need to be present.

### func Varint

```go
func Varint(b []byte) (value, n int, err error)
```

Varint decodes the MQTT variable byte integer at the start of b and returns its value and length. It fails with an incomplete error when b ends inside the integer, and with a malformed one when a fifth byte would be needed (the value would exceed MaxRemaining).

### func WellKnown

```go
func WellKnown(port int) bool
```

WellKnown reports whether port is an MQTT port.

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {
	// S is the session.
	S *wire.Session
	// Level is the protocol level of the CONNECT sent.
	Level byte
	// Ack is the CONNACK, once Connect has succeeded.
```

Client is a minimal, read-only MQTT client session for fingerprinting: it connects, subscribes at QoS 0, reads, unsubscribes and disconnects. It never publishes.



Connect sends a CONNECT of the given level and reads the CONNACK. It returns the session's transport error or wire.ErrClosed when nothing arrived, and a \*NotConnackError when the reply is not a CONNACK valid for the level.


```go

```

#### func (Client) Unsubscribe

```go
func (c *Client) Unsubscribe(filters ...string) bool
```

Unsubscribe sends an UNSUBSCRIBE of the filters and waits, up to the session's idle gap, for the UNSUBACK, discarding the packets before it.

### type Connack

```go
type Connack struct {
	// V5 reports an MQTT 5 CONNACK (reason code and properties); false is
	// the 3.1.1 format (return code).
	V5 bool
	// SessionPresent is the session present flag.
	SessionPresent bool
	// Code is the 3.1.1 return code (0..5) or the MQTT 5 reason code.
	Code byte
	// Properties are the MQTT 5 CONNACK properties.
	Properties Properties
}
```

Connack is a parsed CONNACK.

#### func ParseConnack

```go
func ParseConnack(sent byte, b []byte) (Connack, error)
```

ParseConnack validates b as the answer to a CONNECT of protocol level sent. A 3.1.1 broker answers a CONNECT of either level in the 3.1.1 format (remaining length 2, return code 0..5; an MQTT 5 CONNECT draws return code 1). An MQTT 5 broker answers an MQTT 5 CONNECT in the MQTT 5 format, and may refuse a 3.1.1 CONNECT with reason code 0x84 in the MQTT 5 format. Every other combination, reserved acknowledge flags, a session present flag on a refusal, an unknown code and properties that do not parse exactly are rejected.
